P1:
Flat 2D shadow-theatre cut-out animation, staged like Arabic khayal al-zill and filmed with a 1930s multiplane camera: head, hair, beard and hands are opaque black card with filigree scissor-cut edges; each garment is one flat panel of translucent dyed hide glowing like stained glass, itself the body shape, with no skin showing through. Backlit parchment layers, deep parallax, hard backlight only, noir chiaroscuro, long flat cast shadows, a silent-era tint per shot. The only saturated accent is deep burgundy on his clothing. Film grain, soft vignette, figures animated on twos while snow, smoke and sand drift smoothly. Keep the lower 40% of every frame calm and dark. Flat 2D, not 3D, not CGI. Vertical 9:16.

Four shots of roughly equal length, solemn steady pacing. The narrator is off-screen; the man never speaks. @Image1 defines only the cut-out technique, translucent-hide rendering, paper texture and palette; it contains no person and no clothing.

THE MAN, identical in every shot: broad-shouldered athletic build; a big crown of thick dark wavy-curly hair cut as fine paper tendrils, always readable in his outline; a short dark beard cut as a jagged edge along the jaw; thin wire glasses seen edge-on: only the straight hairline temple arm glints from ear to brow, plus a tiny sliver of rim just in front of the brow line; no circle or ring is ever drawn on the head, and nothing bright sits where an eye would be. His head and face are solid opaque black with no eyes, no eye hole and no features; he is seen only in side profile against light, from behind, or as hands and a cast shadow; he never turns toward the camera; his lips stay closed and still under the beard and his jaw never moves; the voice is an off-screen narrator. In hardship his head bows. Exactly one man in the flesh; other people appear only as faceless cut-out hands or cast shadows that look clearly different from him, never with a curly crown. His clothes change completely at every cut, exactly as written; each shot has one place and one outfit.

Shot 1: A cold stone prison cell, steel-blue, light through a high barred window, one amber lamp. In a grey-brown sackcloth prisoner's tunic with a ragged hem, closed at the neck, iron cuffs and a thin burgundy cord knotted under one cuff, he sits on a stone bench in strict side profile; a cut-out forearm crosses in front of his jaw and hides his mouth while, on the wall behind, the enlarged shadow of huge iron pincers closes and jerks back, a clean small black molar in its jaws. Then the iron door slams and bar shadows sweep across the whole frame.
Shot 2: Hard cut to a bare chamber at dusk, blue-grey, a narrow bright window ahead. In a loose white linen night-thobe, collar closed, he kneels on a reed mat in strict profile; a small bird of pale light, already half drawn out of his chest on a taut glowing thread, slips free and flies out of the window toward a huge sinking cut-paper sun. The sun slides below the sill anyway and blue darkness falls.
Shot 3: Hard cut to a night-blue blizzard, extreme wide, side-on, the figures small on the horizon just below frame centre, the lower part empty snow. In a bulky ochre sheepskin coat with a fleece-fringed outline and a grey wool head-wrap, curls bursting out, snow piling on his shoulders, he leans into the wind leading one balking camel by its halter; in his other hand a small shivering monkey trots behind him on a short leash. No caravan.
Shot 4: Hard cut to a medium side view of a muddy umber tannery under black clouds, limp hides hanging like defeated flags, wavy stink-lines rising from the vats. In a heavy dark leather tanner's apron with crossed straps, one strap burgundy, over a short work tunic, a cloth band across his brow, he heaves a dripping hide onto a wooden frame, then tips his head back in strict profile, still a flat black card shape; the camera tilts up off him to the sky, where a black cut-out cloud closes over the last sliver of sun like a door shutting. The light dies. Hold.

Cuts only at the three shot changes; each cut changes angle and shot size; the camera does not cut on its own. His face always falls in solid black shadow; he never turns toward the camera. Exactly one man in the flesh, fully clothed, his garment covering chest and back. No blood, no injury; hardship only through shadows and objects. The man never speaks; his lips and jaw stay still; no dialogue. No on-screen text, subtitles, letters, numbers, logo, watermark or border. Flat black cut-out silhouettes with translucent dyed-hide garments on glowing parchment; solemn, tragic, never comic; flat 2D, not 3D.

Shot 1: A rocky mountain gorge at night, a huge moon, amber firelight in deep blue. Camera directly behind him at fire level: in an ochre dishdasha hitched at a leather belt, a fur-trimmed hide vest and a head-cloth bound with a faded burgundy cord, he crouches facing a tiny campfire and lowers a skewered roasted lizard with a thick spiky-ringed tail, one bite missing, the bite hidden behind his head; his shoulders heave with disgust, his head still turned to the fire. One continuous pull-back and tilt up: beyond the fire a colossal bear rears on its hind legs, a black silhouette blotting out the moon; he grips his long spear, a toothpick beside it.
Shot 2: Hard cut to a bleached barren field under a white-hot sky, camera at knee height. In a straw-yellow knee-length farmer's tunic, a rope belt, a seed sack across his chest and a straw head-wrap, he strides in strict profile and casts grain in one wide arc; it bounces off the hard ground like pebbles. Across the middle of the frame the cracks are drawn as lips stitched shut, and the last open crack at frame centre presses shut. Nothing grows.
Shot 3: Hard cut to a narrow souq alley at dusk with a clay street brazier glowing red-amber; camera directly behind him at floor level. In a soot-smeared charcoal wool aba over a grey tunic he kneels and blows on the embers; curling smoke rolls back over him and fills the frame. As it clears he walks on bent nearly double, the aba drawn over his head like a hood, a sliver of burgundy lining at its edge; shadows of pointing hands rise on the walls and small faceless hooded shadow figures with no curls turn their backs.
Shot 4: Hard cut to his tall carved brass-studded house door, faded sepia, over the shoulder from behind at hand height. In a long cream merchant's thobe under a faded brown bisht with frayed burgundy trim, he lays a big ornate iron house key into the plump carnelian-ringed hand reaching in from the frame edge. Slow push-in: the fingers snap a tiny copper coin into four and drop one quarter into his open palm with a glint; behind him the carved door swings shut. Hold.

Shot 1: A long sun-baked mud-brick wall by market steps at sunset, hot ochre, wide side-on. In a patched brown traveller's cloak and dusty sirwal, barefoot on hot stones, he hands his last worn boot to a thin bare trader's hand with no rings and receives a flat loaf. On the wall his shadow walks beside a companion's slighter shadow in a tall wound turban with no curls, a water skin on its shoulder; the companion's shadow crumbles into blowing sand and is gone.
Shot 2: Hard cut to a harbour quay at night in a gale, sea-green, a huge billowing sail behind; low angle from behind. In a sea-green porter's vest closed to the collar over a coarse undershirt and a burgundy head-rag, he stands bent under a heavy coil of hawser across his shoulders. The loose end of a giant palm-fibre hawser rears like a sea serpent and slams the sail again and again; its shadow sweeps across the sail and his bent back, and with each swing he sinks lower; gulls scatter. Push onto the rope: it snaps taut and the frame flashes pure white.
Shot 3: From the white, golden dawn: a vast empty flagstone courtyard, high and symmetrical, a slow grand push between foreground pillars on which small shadows of pincers, prison bars, a bear and a coiled rope slide past and fade. A towering dead-black brass-studded door with a ring knocker, a hard lamp-glow above it throwing its shadow toward him. He stands small, back to camera, in his best but plain clothes: a clean pressed white thobe and his one old black bisht with worn, neatly mended gold trim and a glowing burgundy lining. The push ends low over his shoulder: the door's shadow swallows his shadow while his head slowly sinks and his shoulders drop.
Shot 4: Hard cut to a close side view at hand height: his black hand in the burgundy-lined bisht sleeve, already raised a finger's width from the brass knocker, trembles and never touches it. A hatch snaps open; the plump carnelian-ringed hand dangles one coin on a string; his hand lowers. The camera cranes straight up over the top of the door to a high view from behind it: far below, seen only as a crown of curls and a spread bisht, he walks away toward the risen sun, never looking back, rising fully upright; the sun throws his long shadow back across the door. The coin drops unclaimed into the dust; the hatch slams. Hold on the bright courtyard.
